title: The Loss Landscape of XRD-Based Structure Optimization Is Too Rough for Gradient Descent
experiments_summary: Ten crystal structures were selected from the MP20 dataset spanning diverse space groups (e.g., Fm3m, Pm3m, P6/mmm, Cm, etc.). Two types of physically motivated distortions were applied to each structure to generate 50 noisy variants per structure per noise level, yielding 500 distorted inputs per condition: (1) Lattice noise via random strain tensors with diagonal entries sampled uniformly from [1-σ_l, 1+σ_l] and off-diagonal from [-σ_l, σ_l], keeping fractional coordinates fixed; (2) Coordinate noise via i.i.d. Gaussian perturbations N(0, σ_c^2 I_3) added to fractional coordinates modulo 1. Distorted structures were refined using gradient descent through StructSnap, a differentiable XRD simulator based on the kinematic scattering model with Pseudo-Voigt peak profiles and Caglioti broadening, producing 9000-bin diffraction patterns over 2θ ∈ [0°, 90°]. Three loss functions were evaluated: negative cosine similarity, MSE, and negative entropy similarity. Optimization was performed separately for lattice parameters (in response to lattice noise) and atomic coordinates (in response to coordinate noise), with gradients computed via PyTorch autograd. A symmetry-constrained variant of gradient descent was also tested for the lattice-noise case, where each gradient update was followed by projection onto the correct crystal family constraints (e.g., enforcing a=b=c and α=β=γ=90° for cubic). Recovery performance was quantified using Match Rate, defined as the fraction of optimized structures deemed equivalent to the ground truth by StructureMatcher with tolerances of 0.1 for lattice, 0.2 for atomic positions, and 5° for angles. Two-dimensional slices of the optimization landscape were visualized for representative structures (Au2S and Na3MnCoNiO6) to compare unconstrained GD, constrained-initialization GD, and fully constrained GD trajectories. Additionally, structural relaxation using the universal machine learning interatomic potential CHGNet was performed on the same distorted structures as a baseline comparison, and cross-sections of its energy landscape were examined.
